Unit 1:---  Fermentation Processes Fundamentals 
The chronological development of fermentation industry, The range of fermentation 
processes and their producer hosts,  Range of hosts and their genotypes , Basics of 
primary and secondary screening, Strain/host improvement and preservation, 
Microbial and animal cell repositories and procurement protocols 
8 Hrs. 
 
 
 
Unit 2:--- Fermentation Media and Sterilization 
Nutritional requirements for hosts, Basics of microbial and animal cell culturing 
Media components and criteria of their choices, Medium optimization (one factor at a 
time method, statistical methods), Medium sterilization, The design and scale up of 
8 Hrs. 

batch and continuous sterilization processes (Death kinetics, Del factor derivations, 
nutrient quality criterion), Filter sterilization, Large scale sterilization 
Unit 3:--- Inocula Development and Fermentation Processes 
The development of inocula for bacterial, streptomycete, yeast, fungal and animal 
processes, The aseptic inoculation of plant fermenters, Fermentation process 
(Quantifying cell concentration, Quantifying substrates and products), The role of in 
process quality control 
7 Hrs. 
Unit 4:---   Fundamentals of Process Control 
Fundamentals of process control, Components of basic control loop  
Sensors (Temperature, Pressure, Weight, Microbial biomass, Flow rate, Dissolved 
oxygen, Inlet and Exit gas, pH, Rate of stirring), Controllers (Manual and automatic 
controllers), Type of control actions (ON-OFF, Proportional and PID) and Actuators 
Basic fermentation control loops (Temperature, pH, D.O., air flow rate, agitation, 
pressure and antifoam) Loop versus Sequence control   
Case studies (Manual control of fermentation process, Automated controls involving 
event tracking control, logic gates), Operating systems of Bioreactors (SCADA, DCS, 
PLC etc. 
8 Hrs. 
Unit 5:---   Fermentation Process Facility Management  
Clean room Technology (The need and types of Clean rooms,  Basis of Clean room 
Standards, Pharmaceutical Clean room Classification, The Design of Turbulently 
Ventilated and Ancillary Clean rooms- Air supply, High efficiency air filters, Air 
movement within a turbulently ventilated Clean room, Room pressurization and air 
movement control between rooms, Construction materials and finishes. Ancillary 
Clean Rooms (Clothing change area, Material transfer area, Containment Rooms, 
Clean room Testing Clean room Clothing, operating a clean room, clean room 
Disciplines, Methods to Monitor Hazards and Control Methods 
8 Hrs. 
Unit 6:---    Fermentation Broth Handling Strategies  
Broth handling for product recovery - Characterization of fermentation broth, 
Requirements and types of pretreatments (Coagulation, flocculation, cell disruption for 
intracellular products), Biomass and Disrupted Cell Debris Separation  
6 Hrs.

Course Content:  
 
Unit:1 Bioreactor configurations and modes 
Bioreactor configurations, Practical considerations for bioreactor construction, 
Ideal reactor operation, Design of batch bioreactors, Design of fed- batch 
bioreactors 
8 Hrs. 
UNIT:2. Continuous mode of Bioreactors- Design of continuous mode of 
bioreactors, chemostat with immobilized cells, chemostat cascade, chemostat 
with cell recycle, continuous operation of a plug flow reactor, comparison 
between major modes of reactors. 
8 Hrs. 
UNIT:3 Heterogeneous reactions in bioprocesses- 
Introduction, Concentration gradients and reaction rates in solid Catalysts, 
Internal mass transfer and reaction: concentration profile, The Thiele modulus 
8 Hrs. 

and effectiveness factor, External mass transfer, Liquid solid mass transfer 
correlations, Minimizing mass transfer effects 
UNIT:4 Heat and mass transfer in Bioreactor 
Rheology of fermentation broths, Heat transfer in bioreactors: Design equations 
for heat transfer systems. Application of the design equations. Mass transfer in 
bioreactors:  static method and dynamic method, correlation for mass transfer 
co-efficient 
7 Hrs. 
UNIT:5 Scale up of bioreactor 
Scale-up of bioreactors: what is scale up, key variables of biochemical process 
influenced by size, difficulties in scale up, criteria for scale-up, scale-up 
parameters, choice of scale up criteria translation of Biotechnological results to 
different scales, Practice problems 
7 Hrs. 
UNIT:6 Non-ideal reactors: design and analysis 
 Residence time distribution (RTD), earliness and lateness of mixing, Estimation 
of residence time distribution using stimulus experiment and pulse experiment, 
state of aggregation of flowing stream, E curve, F curve, Practice problems. 
7 Hrs.
